disease_label_per_paper: Muckle-Wells syndrome / cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome with recurrent urticaria, fever, hearing loss, and elevated SAA
presentation_summary: 8-year-old girl with intermittent fever for the past year and recurrent raised rash that began around 6 months of age.
Rashes appeared daily, were not itchy, resolved within 1-2 hours without medication, and had no consistent oil, food, drug, insect, or sleep-related pattern.

At age 7 she developed high-grade intermittent fever requiring admission; fever continued despite antitubercular therapy after a positive Mantoux and hilar shadow, while GeneXpert sputum was negative.
Mother had a history of non-pruritic hives, worse during fever and on exposed skin.
Exam showed pallor and well-defined raised lesions; labs showed neutrophilic leukocytosis, anemia, high CRP, elevated ESR, high SAA, and audiometry showed severe hearing loss.
NLRP3 germline mutation, clinical diagnosis, anti-histamine nonresponse, TB misdiagnosis, and planned biologic therapy are preserved as confirmatory or non-ranking context.
